title: A fourth far-pointer argument is assigned a 16-bit RS pair
summary: In the default far-pointer calling convention (Imag32), CC_MOS offers a far (addrspace 2) pointer only RL1..RL3 and has no fallback of its own. A fourth far-pointer argument falls through to the generic CCIfPtr rule and receives a free 16-bit RSn pair. The machine verifier rejects the resulting 32-bit COPY from a 16-bit register; the downstream release build without the verifier crashes with a segmentation fault. The same holds in plain mosw65816 and under +mos-a16. Found by the independent review of the extracted far series (finding B1) and reproduced on the downstream toolchain.

unknowns: Plain mosw65816 (no +mos-a16): call lowering now stacks the fourth far pointer correctly, but reading that 4-byte stacked value back fails with "unable to legalize G_MERGE_VALUES s32" (candidate-plain-w65816.log). This is the existing plain-mode limitation for any far-pointer value in memory (a far-pointer load from a near global fails identically on the baseline); it is loud, not silent. Making far-pointer values in memory legal without +mos-a16 is a separate design decision.

The opt-in +mos-farcc-split and +mos-farcc-axy variants also reach the new fallback, but they already abort on the baseline whenever a custom-assigned far pointer is followed by another argument, before any exhaustion (docs/defects/mos-far-cc-split-axy-custom-args.json); no regression covers them here.

prior_work.source_assessment: Downstream MOSCallingConv.td gates four far-pointer rules on MOSSubtarget::farPtrCC(). The default Imag32 rule is CCAssignToReg<[RL1, RL2, RL3]> with no stack fallback; only the opt-in Stack variant (+mos-farcc-stack) assigns CCAssignToStack<4, 1>. The extracted patch 4 keeps only the RL rule. Neither falls back when the quads are taken.
prior_work.binary_assessment: Downstream release llc 9031686c exits 134 with the verifier and 139 (SIGSEGV) without it; the extracted assertions candidate d7fde754 fails the same verifier check or asserts in RegisterBankInfo.cpp:569.
prior_work.decision: The September 28 packet listed far-pointer ABI register exhaustion as an open contract to review; no defect record, TODO item or patch covers it. New canonical record.

configuration.expected: the fourth far pointer is passed on the soft stack

baseline.failure_signature: Copy Instruction is illegal with mismatching sizes

resolution.change: patches/llvm-mos/0002-321-accum16.patch: MOSCallingConv.td adds an ungated CCIfPtrAddrSpace<2, CCAssignToStack<4, 1>> after the four farPtrCC()-gated far-pointer rules and before the direct-page and generic CCIfPtr rules.
resolution.causal_explanation: CC_MOS gave a far pointer only the selected variant's registers (RL1..RL3 for the default Imag32) and no fallback, so a fourth far pointer fell through to CCIfPtr<CCAssignToReg<[RS1..RS7]>> and took a free 16-bit RS pair; the 32-bit COPY from it is malformed. The new rule assigns a far pointer that found no register a 4-byte soft-stack slot, which the existing Stack-variant store/load path in MOSCallLowering already handles, so the pointer never reaches the 16-bit rule. Arguments that fit in registers are assigned exactly as before.
resolution.trigger_check: The unchanged abi4.ll runs through the candidate llc with the baseline configuration (mosw65816, +mos-a16, O2, -verify-machineinstrs) and exits 0; the baseline llc aborts with the verifier's mismatching-size COPY on the same command.
